digest.component_or_area: lifecycle cascade table and concurrency model
propositions: The _CASCADING_EDGES table's one-eligible-status-per-edge shape does not prevent two reachable residuals: reactivating a closed child under an open parent (no cascade), and blocked→in_progress resume under an open parent (no cascade).

The store-level invariant 'no non-terminal-state ticket can be a child of a closed ticket' is enforced jointly by the cascade table's closed-source rows and the unconditional open-children close guard in transition_close.py, not by a total status ordering predicate.

The docs/concurrency.md §I4a headline sentence 'A child never runs ahead of its parent in the lifecycle' overstates the table's guarantee and must be narrowed to the per-edge, same-edge guarantee it actually provides.

The blocked→in_progress transition fires the start-work gate but does not cascade (gate and cascade answer different questions); this disagreement must be resolved as documented non-cascading in the table comments and docs alongside the gate note.
No transition refused today becomes permitted; the claim-status guard (txn.claim_core) remains untouched; all existing cascade tests pass with the documentation and comment changes only.
